output.name: Halun — The Full Beak
output.myth: Halun was a puffin who fished the cold water under the cliffs for chicks that were always hungry. One winter Tavo the Gale came down the bay and shook the sea like a sail, and no bird could fly into it. Halun went anyway. He dived where the sand-eels hide and came up with his beak full, the silver eels laid crossways so he could not speak. He flew home against the wind with the catch held shut. His chicks ran to him and he gave them everything and said nothing. Aun asked him why he would not sing out his luck. Halun opened his beak, and the eels slid and shone. Hesk, who keeps count, wound a line for him and set him in the Windward Reach, a fist east of the Torn Sleeve and nearly two fists west of the grey Oil-Spitter, who keeps her oil in her gut and never speaks. Mothers say that when your father comes in with cold hands and nothing to say, you do not ask him. You take the fish.
output.finding: From the Torn Sleeve, look a little under a fist east along the Windward Reach to find Halun, with his mouth full.
